newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ASPRILLA AND GOALKEEPERS KEEP ON SCORING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ASPRILLA AND GOALKEEPERS KEEP ON SCORING.

text.p: Striker Faustino Asprilla continued to thrive in the Colombian national team while yet another goalkeeper got on the scoresheet as South America's intriguing World Cup qualifiers continued on Wednesday.
Asprilla scored for the sixth time in five qualifiers as Colombia beat neighbours Ecuador 1-0 away to go four points clear at the top of the single nine-team group.
Venezuela goalkeeper Rafael Dudamel emulated Paraguay's Jose Luis Chilavert, who last month gave his country a 1-1 draw away to Argentina by scoring direct from a free kick.
The Argentines were again on the receiving end but, despite trailing for half an hour in the first half to the continent's minnows, eventually won 5-2.

Paraguay continued their impressive form with a 2-1 win at home to Chile while Uruguay, who like Argentina had struggled in previous matches, scored a crucial win 1-0 over Bolivia on Tuesday thanks to an own goal by hapless defender Juan Manuel Pena.

The new format, in which all the countries play each other twice, continued to pull in the fans, who appear to be appreciating the chance to see South America's top stars perform regularly in their own continent.

Venezuela, where soccer is a poor second to baseball in popularity, still managed to attract 30,000 people to their game in the provincial town of San Cristobal, nearly twice the crowd in soccer-mad Italy that watched their team play Georgia earlier on Wednesday in Perugia.
Paraguay and Ecuador were watched by more than 40,000 each, while 70,000 saw Uruguay's game in the Centenario stadium.

Asprilla, whose clever flicks often appear to outwit his own team-mates when he plays with his English club Newcastle United, has been revelling in the monthly matches with players who were brought up playing the same one-touch soccer as he was.
His goal in the 62nd minute ended a 100 percent home record for Ecuador, who are coached by Colombia's Francisco Maturana, a man who has had a huge influence on Colombian soccer in the last decade.
Ecuador, who have never reached the World Cup finals, stayed second thanks to three previous home wins, including one against Argentina.
Argentina, who had not won any of their previous three games, fell behind to a seventh-minute goal by Giovanni Savarese against opponents they once beat 11-0 in 1975.

Ariel Ortega finally equalised in the 35th minute after a defensive mistake and in the second half Argentina finally asserted their authority with goals by Juan Sorin, Diego Simeone, Hugo Morales and Jose Albornoz.
Dudamel's amazing strike from outside the penalty area came in the 87th minute. The result moved Argentina into third place and kept Venezuela rooted to the bottom.
Chilavert did not have a chance to increase his goalscoring tally as Paraguay came from behind to beat Chile with goals by central defenders Carlos Gamarra and Catalino Rivarola.

Paraguay, who have already beaten Uruguay away, moved into fourth place and, with the inspirational leadership of the flamboyant Chilavert, look capable of reaching the World Cup finals for the first time since 1986.
The top four teams go through to the 1998 finals in France. Brazil qualify automatically as world champions.
